name: Salt and Treason
summary: Chapter 2 of The Seven Teeth of Vashkul. Almonry relief grain is spreading the Whispering Sickness through Port Sorrel, Governor Pell takes Choir bribes and blames pirates, and the Choir smuggler Harrow Vey races for two Teeth: the Brass Tooth in the Brass Parrot vault and the Singing Tooth of the sea hag of the Singing Reef. The hero must choose between the Saltwind Company, the Red Gull Brotherhood and their own course.

chapters.name: Salt and Treason
chapters.summary: Uncover the plague grain in Port Sorrel, save (or lose) Rook at Fort Kestrel, choose a side at the Grinning Coin, settle Gullhaven, race Harrow Vey for the Brass and Singing Teeth, and bring Governor Pell to his reckoning.

scenes.name: The Quarantine Docks of Port Sorrel
scenes.seed: Port Sorrel's whitewashed harbor flies yellow quarantine flags. Iron cages of 'pirates' hang along the quay, and Almonry relief ships swing crates of grain ashore, each stamped with a wheat-sheaf under a crown. Saltwind clerks tally everything twice.

variants.seed: The quay lamps are lit and the bonded warehouse is shuttered, but a few dockworkers never seem to go home.
Fen refugees who fled the Warden pyres of Hollowmere beg along the quay.
A few Hollowmere refugees sit apart on the quay, humming the Choir’s tune without noticing.
A Briarkin healer from Hollowmere sells cure-tea by the fish market; word of the fen's cure has reached the coast.
You know the Sickness' signs now: there is grey dust in the seams of the grain sacks.
Mother Sallow's manifest in your pack lists these very ships by name.
In a dockside grog-shop a sailor boasts that Captain Vey's patrons already hold 'teeth from the fen'.
Nettle wrinkles her nose at the grain. "Smells like the Abbey undercroft," she mutters.
Ser Corwin eyes the hanging cages with open distaste.
Saltwind wanted posters on the harbor wall bear a fair likeness of you.
Company clerks tip their hats to you now.
The Saltwind board is sitting at Company House today, and Governor Pell has doubled his guard.
A grey-sailed boat is gone from the Governor's private mooring.

onEnter.text: A Saltwind crier reads the day’s justice from the harbor steps: the pirate Rook Marrowby hangs at Fort Kestrel before this time tomorrow. On the next quay, Almonry relief ships are unloading grain for the fever wards.

pois.name: The Almonry grain crates
pois.seed: Relief grain in sealed crates, stamped with the Almonry wheat-sheaf and the crown. Some sacks leak a fine grey dust.

actions.label: Inspect the grain crates

success.text: Under the wheat-sheaf is a second, smaller seal: the private mark of the Royal Almonry. The grain is furred with grey Maw-rot spores.

failure.text: The crates look like honest relief grain to you, and a clerk shoos you away from them.

advantageIf.source: You know the Sickness' spore signs
Nettle's nose for Maw-rot

actions.label: Match Sallow's manifest to the crates

outcome.text: The ship names and crate numbers match Sallow's manifest exactly. Under the wheat-sheaf is the Almonry's private seal, and the grain is furred with grey spores.

pois.name: The harbor cages
pois.seed: Sunburnt men in iron cages over the water, under a sign that reads PIRATES.

actions.label: Talk to the caged "pirates"

outcome.text: They are fishermen who could not pay the tariff. One whispers that the grain that makes people sing comes ashore at night, off Captain Harrow Vey's ships.

actions.label: Accept Governor Pell's welcome

outcome.text: Governor Pell greets you in person, perfumed and smiling. He blames the fever on pirate grain, offers "every courtesy of the Company", and twists a ring that looks very new.

actions.label: Wait on the quay until dark

outcome.text: You nurse a mug in a quayside grog-shop until the lamps are lit.

actions.label: Slip into the bonded warehouse

success.text: You slip between the stacks unseen and find the Choir at work: dockworkers resealing sacks by lantern-light. You have the first blow.

failure.text: A board creaks. The dockworkers drop their sacks and draw knives.

advantageIf.source: Pell's own warehouse pass

disadvantageIf.source: Pell has doubled the warehouse watch

actions.label: Search the bonded warehouse

outcome.text: Opened sacks bear the Almonry’s private seal, and the grain is thick with grey spores. A tally-slate lists "the Captain’s" next run to the Brass Parrot.

actions.label: Report the Choir cell to the Saltwind Company

outcome.text: A Company factor counts the bodies, pays the bounty and writes your name in a very good ledger.

exits.label: Ride the coast road to Fort Kestrel
Take a fishing boat to Fennick's Rest
Go to Company House and confront Governor Pell

revisitSeed: The quarantine docks of Port Sorrel again: gulls, tar and the crier's bell.
Back on the Port Sorrel quay, where the cages still hold fishermen who could not pay the tariff.

scenes.name: The Gallows of Fort Kestrel
scenes.seed: A star-shaped Saltwind fort bristles on its bluff above a long row of gallows. In a cage cell by the gate, a tiefling in a ruined silk coat sings rude shanties about the Governor. Commander Lusk watches the road and fingers his purse.

variants.seed: Your wanted poster is pinned beside Lusk’s door. There will be no bribing him today.
An oyster-seller in a red kerchief by the gate catches your eye and winks.
The noon drums are rolling. A procession marches Rook Marrowby toward the gallows.
Rook's cage is empty. A new rope sways on the gallows row.
You are in the cell next to Rook’s. He grins through the bars: "Welcome to the finest lodgings in the Isles."
The garrison is still turning the fort upside down looking for its missing pirate.
Lusk waves to you from the scaffold like an old friend.

pois.name: Rook's effects
pois.seed: A clerk's crate of a hanged man's things: a silk coat, loaded dice, a folded scrap of oilcloth.

actions.label: Lift the half-map from the effects crate

success.text: The oilcloth is half a treasure map, inked with a parrot and a volcano. It is yours now.

failure.text: The clerk slams the crate shut and calls for the guard. You leave empty-handed.

actions.label: Talk to the singing prisoner

outcome.text: Rook swears he is no pirate: he saw what Captain Harrow Vey unloads at night, grain that makes people sing, and the Governor wants him quiet. He also knows half of the Brass Parrot map, "tattooed on my memory, friend."

actions.label: Bribe Commander Lusk (50 gp)

success.text: Fifty gold changes hands ("a processing fee," Lusk says), and Rook is released into your custody. He recites his half of the map before he is out of the gate.

failure.text: Lusk weighs you, weighs the purse, and decides the Governor pays better. You are shown the gate.

advantageIf.source: Lusk has taken a liking to you

actions.label: Bribe Lusk with a tall tale (50 gp)

success.text: You tell Lusk the Company board wants Rook alive as a witness, and fifty gold makes the story true enough. Rook walks out with you, reciting his half of the map.

failure.text: Lusk laughs in your face and keeps the door shut.

advantageIf.source: Lusk has taken a liking to you

actions.label: Present forged release papers

success.text: Lusk reads your forged release order twice, salutes it, and hands Rook over. Rook bows to the Commander on his way out, just to watch him seethe.

failure.text: Lusk holds the forgery up to the light and tears it in half. You leave before he looks too hard at you.

actions.label: Present forged release papers under a false name

success.text: Hat low and name borrowed, you hand over a forged release order. Lusk never looks up from the seal. Rook strolls out beside you.

failure.text: Lusk glances from the order to your poster and back. You are gone before he finishes shouting.

actions.label: Buy oysters from the red-kerchiefed seller

outcome.text: The oyster-seller is a Red Gull. "Spring Rook and the Brotherhood forgives a hundred of what you owe," she murmurs, and sketches the night guard rota on a shell.

actions.label: Wait in the fort village until nightfall

outcome.text: You kill the hours in the fort village, watching the guard change.

actions.label: Creep into the cell block at night

success.text: You go over the seaward wall between rounds and reach the cell block unseen.

failure.text: A sentry’s lantern swings your way. "Alarm! Over the wall!"

advantageIf.source: The Red Gulls’ guard rota
You know when the seaward watch changes

actions.label: Creep into the cell block at night (the garrison knows your face)

success.text: You go over the seaward wall between rounds and reach the cell block unseen.

failure.text: A sentry knows your face from the posters. "Alarm! It’s the outlaw!"

advantageIf.source: The Red Gulls’ guard rota
You know when the seaward watch changes

actions.label: Pick the lock of Rook's cell (thieves' tools)

success.text: The lock gives with a click. Rook kisses the bars goodbye, whispers his half of the map, and follows you over the wall.

failure.text: A pick snaps with a sound like a pistol shot. Boots pound on the stairs.

actions.label: Storm the gallows and cut Rook down

outcome.text: You vault onto the scaffold as the drums stop. The garrison comes for you.

actions.label: Let the hanging go ahead

outcome.text: The drums stop. Rook Marrowby makes a joke nobody hears and drops. A clerk carries his effects to the gatehouse.

actions.label: Break out of the cells with Rook

success.text: You and Rook work a loose bar free together and drop into the surf below the fort. You are both outlaws now, and he is grinning.

failure.text: The bars hold. You sit out three days until Lusk tires of feeding you and throws you out with a fine.

actions.label: Break out of the cells

success.text: You work a loose bar free and drop into the surf below the fort. Escaping makes you an outlaw.

failure.text: The bars hold. You sit out three days until Lusk tires of feeding you and throws you out with a fine.

exits.label: Walk the smugglers' path to Fennick's Rest

revisitSeed: Fort Kestrel again, the gallows black against the sky.
Back under Fort Kestrel's walls, where the gulls wait on the scaffold beam.

scenes.name: The Grinning Coin at Fennick's Rest
scenes.seed: Painted shacks crowd a cheerful harbor, and every lane leads to the Grinning Coin, a gambling hall built from a beached galleon. At the knucklebones table, Quint's quartermaster Jory Flint has staked half a treasure map: a parrot, a volcano, and a lot of ocean.

variants.seed: The hall roars. Captain Marisol "Two-Hats" Quint holds court at the back, one hat stacked on the other.
Half the hall shouts Rook’s name and the other half checks its purse.
The Red Gulls drink a sour toast to Rook Marrowby, hanged at Kestrel.
The quiet man nursing one drink by the door wears Saltwind boots under his fisherman’s smock.
Flint eyes you sourly over his empty stake.
The stool by the door where the Company man sat is empty. Flint wears a new pair of Saltwind boots.
Someone at the bar is still telling the story of your drinking match with Quint.

actions.label: Play knucklebones against Flint (round 1)

success.text: You read Flint's tell and take round 1.

failure.text: Flint's bones come up sixes. Round 1 to the quartermaster.

advantageIf.source: Rook told you Flint's tell

actions.label: Play knucklebones against Flint (round 2)

success.text: You read Flint's tell and take round 2.

failure.text: Flint's bones come up sixes. Round 2 to the quartermaster.

advantageIf.source: Rook told you Flint's tell

actions.label: Play knucklebones against Flint (round 3)

success.text: You read Flint's tell and take round 3.

failure.text: Flint's bones come up sixes. Round 3 to the quartermaster.

advantageIf.source: Rook told you Flint's tell

actions.label: Cheat at knucklebones

success.text: Your bones roll kings every time. Flint pays up the half-map with the face of a man who knows and cannot prove it.

failure.text: A loaded bone skitters across the table and lands under Flint’s nose. The hall goes quiet, then very loud.

actions.label: Watch the hall for Company eyes

success.text: The quiet man by the door is no fisherman: Saltwind boots, a clerk’s ink-stained cuffs.

failure.text: Everyone here looks like a pirate to you.

actions.label: Share a drink with Captain Quint

outcome.text: Quint swaps hats and leans in. "Pell hangs our lads and eats the Choir’s silver. Expose him, and the Brotherhood sails with you."

actions.label: Wait at the Grinning Coin until evening

outcome.text: You while away the day watching fishermen bet on gull races.

actions.label: Hear out the Saltwind agent

outcome.text: Factor Ashcombe keeps his voice low. "Lead the Company to Gullhaven. We will rewrite your debts and name you Captain-Agent, with a Company gunboat under you."

actions.label: Swear in with the Red Gull Brotherhood

outcome.text: Quint hugs Rook ("cousin-in-law, you disgrace!") and spits in her palm to shake on it. At her nod, Flint hands over his half of the map.

actions.label: Win Captain Quint’s trust

success.text: Quint spits in her palm and shakes. At her nod, Flint hands over his half of the map.

failure.text: "Come back when you’ve done something for the Isles," Quint says, and turns her hats away.

advantageIf.source: You matched Quint drink for drink

actions.label: Take the Company’s commission

outcome.text: Ashcombe slides a sealed commission across the table. A Company gunboat will meet you at sea, and Gullhaven is to be "brought to order".

actions.label: Sail under your own colors

outcome.text: You drink to nobody’s cause. Gullhaven’s free harbor will take anyone’s coin, including yours.

exits.label: Take the smugglers’ path to Fort Kestrel

revisitSeed: The Grinning Coin again: smoke, dice and a hundred lies told at once.
Back at Fennick's Rest, where the knucklebones never stop clicking.

scenes.name: The Gullhaven Truce
scenes.seed: Gullhaven floats on the hulls of a hundred wrecks lashed together over a lagoon. Pirates, traders and shipwrights share the grog-houses under a truce as thin as sailcloth. Harbormaster Oswin Tull, a round and cheerful gnome, knows every tide and every rumor, and sells both.

variants.seed: Red Gull sails crowd the lagoon. Lookouts shout that a Saltwind squadron is on the horizon.
Company marines are at your back, and Gullhaven knows it. The grog-houses empty onto the decks with cutlasses out, led by a scarred woman called Iron Jenny.
Everyone is watching everyone. The truce holds, for now.
Company flags fly from every mast. The shipwrights work under guard.
Half the port is charred timber hissing in the lagoon.
Rook knows every grog-house by name and owes most of them money.
Company marines stand on the lashings, but no hull is burned and no blood was spilled.
The Tidewright bargemen turn their backs as you pass.

actions.label: Ask Harbormaster Tull about the Singing Reef

outcome.text: Tull’s chart of the Singing Reef is the only safe one in the Isles: a hundred gold, or a favor. "And be quick," he adds. "Harrow Vey’s been buying charts too."

actions.label: Haggle over the chart

success.text: Tull laughs and halves the price: "for the entertainment."

failure.text: Tull’s smile doesn’t move and neither does his price.

actions.label: Buy the reef chart

outcome.text: Coin changes hands and Tull rolls the chart into an oilcloth tube.

actions.label: Study the parrot riddles in the harbor library

success.text: The Brass Parrot’s riddles all come from one book: the almanac of the vanished tinkerer Hobb Brasswick. You copy the key pages.

failure.text: The library is a heap of water-stained logbooks. Nothing useful.

actions.label: Trade Old Sal Brine a bottle of rum for his stories

outcome.text: Old Sal drinks half the bottle and taps his scarred ear. "Auntie Brackwater sings. Don’t listen to the pretty part, and never promise her what you remember."

actions.label: Lead the Company raid on Gullhaven

outcome.text: Company marines storm the decks behind you, and Iron Jenny’s militia meets you at the lashings.

actions.label: Defend Gullhaven from the Saltwind squadron

outcome.text: Saltwind longboats grind against the outer hulls, and marines come over the rails.

actions.label: Run the Saltwind blockade for Tull

outcome.text: You run Tidewright letters past the Saltwind pickets by night. Tull pays in charts: the reef chart, and his own tide-tables for the fast currents between the reef and the Brass Parrot.

actions.label: Cast off without Tull’s favor

outcome.text: You leave Gullhaven to its thin truce and put to sea.

exits.label: Sail for the Isle of Brass Parrots by the map
Search the southern islands for the Brass Parrot with half a map

failure.text: A day lost among the wrong volcanoes.

revisitSeed: Gullhaven again, its lashed hulls creaking on the lagoon.
Back among the rope bridges of Gullhaven, where Tull's lantern burns in the harbor office.

scenes.name: The Caves of Wreckers' Cove
scenes.seed: Sea caves where wreckers once lured ships onto the rocks with false lights. The Red Gulls stash loot in the outer caverns; deeper in, behind a rusted grate, Harrow Vey’s smugglers keep a stash room of their own. The tide comes in fast here.

variants.seed: Red Gull guards wave you through with a wink: the Brotherhood wants Vey’s stash as much as you do.
Vey’s stash room is open and dripping. The tide is rising.
You have marked the false lights and the tide line: you know how long you have.

actions.label: Look for false lights and read the tide

success.text: Two of the lanterns in the cave mouth are wreckers’ false lights on chains. The water line on the walls says you have about an hour before the tide.

failure.text: Lights, water, rock. It all looks the same in the dark.

advantageIf.source: Quint told you which lights are false

actions.label: Break into Vey’s stash room

outcome.text: Behind the grate, Vey’s first mate "Salt-Eye" Mora and her smugglers look up from their dice. So does a treasure chest with too many teeth.

actions.label: Open Vey’s stash room

outcome.text: The Gulls have run Vey’s smugglers off; the stash room is unguarded but for one handsome sea-chest. It yawns.

actions.label: Decipher the Choir ledger

success.text: A simple cipher of hymn numbers. Every payment to Governor Pell is marked "per the Almonry", and the ledger is initialled S.V.

failure.text: The cipher is hymn numbers and nonsense to you. The ledger itself is still evidence.

actions.label: Let Aurek read the Choir ledger

outcome.text: Aurek reads the hymn-number cipher at a glance, then goes very quiet: every payment to Pell is "per the Almonry", initialled S.V.

actions.label: Give the Red Gulls their half of the stash

outcome.text: You leave the Brotherhood’s half on the tally-rock. Word of an honest share travels fast in the Isles.

actions.label: Keep the whole stash

outcome.text: You pocket the Brotherhood’s half too. Somebody will notice.

actions.label: Climb out before the tide

success.text: You haul yourself up the chimney as the sea roars into the stash room below.

failure.text: The tide catches you in the chimney. You come out an hour later, half-drowned and bruised.

advantageIf.source: You read the tide

scenes.revisitSeed: The caves of Wreckers' Cove again, the sea breathing in and out of the dark.

scenes.name: The Singing Reef
scenes.seed: A ring of coral spires hums as the wind rises, a low sweet chord that tugs at the ear. In the still lagoon at its heart stands a stilt hut hung with fishbones and wind-chimes: the home of the sea hag Auntie Brackwater, who keeps the Singing Tooth.

variants.seed: Tull’s chart marks a safe channel through the spires.
Your ship lists on the coral with a hole in her side.
Someone has been here first: chum slicks the water, sharks circle, and the hut’s shelf where the Tooth sat is empty.
The Singing Tooth hums in your pack in harmony with the reef.
The hut is silent. The reef still sings.

actions.label: Steer through the coral spires without a chart

success.text: You read the swell and the colour of the water and thread the spires into the lagoon.

failure.text: Coral tears the hull. You limp into the lagoon holed and scattered; when the fight comes, it will find your party split.

actions.label: Brace against the reef’s song

success.text: You hear the pretty part of the song and do not listen to it.

failure.text: The song is so kind. You are waist-deep in the lagoon before a companion’s shout breaks the spell (charmed until the end of your first turn if a fight starts here).

advantageIf.source: Old Sal’s warning

actions.label: Trade a year of your memories for the Singing Tooth

outcome.text: Auntie Brackwater lays a cold hand on your temple and sings a year of your life out through your ear. (You lose one skill proficiency of your choice until it is restored.) Coral-scale patterning spreads over your temple. She drops the Singing Tooth into your palm.

actions.label: Fight Auntie Brackwater for the Tooth

outcome.text: Auntie Brackwater laughs like a drain, and two merrow haul themselves out of the lagoon at her call.

actions.label: Make the hag pay for helping Vey

outcome.text: "Vey paid in blood, dearie. You’ll pay the same." The merrow rise, and the sharks turn toward you.

exits.label: Ride the fast currents to the Isle of Brass Parrots
Sail the long way round to the Isle of Brass Parrots

scenes.name: The Vault of the Brass Parrot
scenes.seed: A jungle island under a smoking volcano. Clockwork parrots squawk riddles from the trees. At the mountain’s foot, three brass doors shaped like parrot heads seal the vault of a vanished tinkerer, and Captain Harrow Vey’s Choir expedition is digging at the first of them.

variants.seed: Quint’s crew holds the beach behind you. No Choir reinforcements will land today.
A Company gunboat rides at anchor in the bay; its marines are waiting to "secure the treasure".
You are too late. The doors hang open and the vault is stripped; Vey’s ship is a sail on the horizon.
Broken armor and bent brass swords litter the vault floor.
Vey’s diggers wear seven-tooth sigils and sing while they work.
Salt-Eye Mora waits at the jungle's edge, knife loose in its sheath.

actions.label: Cut through the jungle to the volcano

success.text: You find the tinkerer’s old road under the vines and reach the volcano in a day.

failure.text: Two days of vines, rain and riddling parrots before you reach the volcano.

actions.label: Answer the riddle of door 1

success.text: The parrot asks what runs but never walks; you answer "the tide". The brass door swings open.

failure.text: Wrong answer. Fire jets from the parrot’s beak before the door grinds open anyway.

advantageIf.source: Brasswick's almanac

actions.label: Answer the riddle of door 2

success.text: The parrot asks which king drowned in his own harbor; you name him. The brass door swings open.

failure.text: Wrong answer. Fire jets from the parrot’s beak before the door grinds open anyway.

advantageIf.source: Brasswick's almanac

actions.label: Answer the riddle of door 3

success.text: The parrot asks what grows by being taken away; you answer "a hole". The brass door swings open.

failure.text: Wrong answer. Fire jets from the parrot’s beak before the door grinds open anyway.

advantageIf.source: Brasswick's almanac

actions.label: Enter the treasure vault

outcome.text: Gems heaped in brass bowls, a brass-buttoned cape on a stand, and on an altar a dark tooth the size of a thumb. Suits of armor step off their plinths, and brass swords rise, squawking.

actions.label: Face Harrow Vey at the vault door

outcome.text: "I’ll take that tooth, darling," says Harrow Vey, all charm and pistols, and his Choir diggers close in behind him.

actions.label: Face Harrow Vey at the vault door

outcome.text: Quint’s crew has pinned Vey’s diggers on the beach. Harrow Vey comes up the vault road alone, all charm and pistols.

actions.label: Take Harrow Vey prisoner

outcome.text: You bind Vey hand and foot. He compliments the knots.

actions.label: Finish Harrow Vey

outcome.text: Harrow Vey yields, and you kill him anyway. The parrots fall silent for a moment.

actions.label: Divide the treasure with Quint’s crew

outcome.text: The Brotherhood carries the gems down to the boats singing, and Quint counts out your share with scrupulous flourish.

actions.label: Let the Company marines claim the treasure

outcome.text: The marines crate the gems "for the Company’s audit" and hand you a finder’s fee and a receipt.

actions.label: Claim the treasure and give Rook a fair share

outcome.text: You split the gems down the middle of a sail. Rook stares at his heap as if it might vanish.

actions.label: Claim the whole Brass Parrot treasure

outcome.text: A thousand gold in gems goes into your packs.

actions.label: Search the stripped vault

outcome.text: Vey’s diggers were thorough. You find a few gems trodden into the floor and a note in Vey’s hand: "Port Sorrel, the Governor’s birthday."

exits.label: Ride the fast currents to the Singing Reef
Sail the long way round to the Singing Reef

scenes.name: Pell's Reckoning
scenes.seed: Company House overlooks the harbor, all white columns and golden scales. The Saltwind board is in session in the long room, and Governor Cassius Pell is smiling at them. Out on the water, grey boats with hooded lanterns are gliding toward the quay.

variants.seed: Two Company guards fall in beside you: the board has been told to expect you.
Red Gull sails idle just outside the harbor chain, waiting for your signal.
Harrow Vey’s ship is among the grey boats, flying the Choir’s seven-tooth pennant.
You carry the Almonry seal’s evidence and the Choir ledger. Pell has nowhere left to stand.
Pell sits in irons before his own board.
Pell’s private sloop is a white speck on the horizon.
A royal courier waits on the steps with a letter under the Queen’s own seal: Isolde summons you to Highcrown.
Pell’s letters point to Highcrown, where your face is on the wanted posters. You will have to sneak in.
Somewhere out on the water a grey sail waits. Harrow Vey keeps his promises too.

actions.label: Lay the seal and the ledger before the board

outcome.text: You lay out the Almonry seal and the Choir ledger. Pell goes grey, and then he confesses: Choir silver, every month, to look away from the grain.

actions.label: Present the Choir ledger

outcome.text: The ledger lists Pell’s payments line by line. Before his own board, he breaks and confesses.

actions.label: Lean on Pell until he confesses

success.text: Pell’s smile cracks. In front of the board, he admits the Choir’s silver bought his silence about the grain.

failure.text: Pell only laughs and calls you a pirate’s lackey. The board looks uneasy all the same.

advantageIf.source: The Almonry seal
You saw the Almonry seal on Pell's ring

actions.label: Hold the quay against the Choir

outcome.text: Cultists pour off the grey boats with knives and hymns, led by a Choir captain with a boarding axe. They have come to silence Pell, and you are in the way.

actions.label: Hold the quay against Vey and the Choir

outcome.text: Harrow Vey leaps onto the quay in a new captain’s coat, pistols in both hands, and the Choir pours off the grey boats behind him.

actions.label: Chase the fleeing Governor

success.text: You catch Pell on the gangplank of his private sloop and haul him back by his perfumed collar.

failure.text: Pell’s sloop slips its mooring with him aboard. The Governor has fled.

advantageIf.source: Pell has not slept since you warned him

actions.label: Search Pell's dispatch case

outcome.text: Pell’s letters are signed only with initials, and every one ends the same way: "S.V., the Almonry, Highcrown."

actions.label: Put the case against Pell to the Saltwind board

success.text: The board votes, one by one, and Pell is arrested by his own Company. The board pays you its reward.

failure.text: The board dithers, and in the dithering Pell’s friends buy him a boat. By nightfall the Governor has fled.

advantageIf.source: Pell confessed
Pell's letters
You saw the Almonry seal on Pell's ring
Ashcombe warned the board

disadvantageIf.source: Pell shows the board the purse you took from him

actions.label: Offer Pell silence if he turns on the Choir

outcome.text: Pell takes the deal before you finish offering it. He will stay Governor, and the Choir’s grain ships will find every Company port closed.

actions.label: Kill Governor Pell

outcome.text: You kill Governor Pell on the steps of Company House, in front of the board and half the harbor. The Saltwind Company will call it murder.

actions.label: Petition the board to lift the occupation of Gullhaven

success.text: With Pell in irons, the board has no appetite for his war. The marines are recalled from Gullhaven.

failure.text: The board will not give up a prize port. Gullhaven stays occupied.

advantageIf.source: You know the board's own orders for Gullhaven

npcs.personality: A smiling, perfumed administrator with a ledger for a heart. Hangs pirates on Tuesdays and dines with smugglers on Fridays.
secrets: Takes monthly Choir silver to look away from the Almonry grain.

npcs.name: Auntie Brackwater
npcs.personality: The sea hag of the Singing Reef: grandmotherly, greedy and hungry for memories, which she keeps in jars of seawater.
secrets: Holds the Singing Tooth and would sell it to anyone who pays in memories or blood.
npcs.voice: Crooning and wet; calls everyone "dearie"; hums the reef’s chord under her words.

nodes.text: *Jars of seawater clink on every shelf of her coral hut, each with a memory swimming in it.* "Something to trade, dearie?"

options.label: "A year is too dear, Auntie. A summer."

success.text: Auntie Brackwater sighs and takes only a summer: the smell of a kitchen, the name of a childhood friend. You keep your skills. She drops the Singing Tooth into your palm.

failure.text: "A year, dearie, or nothing. I am not a fishwife."

options.label: Offer her a year you never lived

advantageIf.source: Old Sal told you how she listens

success.text: You sing her a year of storms and sweethearts that never happened. She drinks it down, delighted, and pays in coral. By the time she tastes the lie you are over the reef with the Singing Tooth.

failure.text: Auntie Brackwater spits out the false memory like a bad oyster. "Cheat!" The merrow rise at her call.

options.label: "Take a year of Rook's memories instead."

outcome.text: Rook stares at you, then walks into the lagoon without a word and lets her sing. When he comes out he cannot remember his mother's face. She drops the Singing Tooth into your palm.

options.label: "I'll think about it, Auntie."

nodes.text: "Come back when you have more to forget."
The lagoon boils.
